tfResources.role: Primary/required resource. Carries nearly every CfnQueueProps field directly as top-level attributes (content_based_deduplication, deduplication_scope, delay_seconds, fifo_queue, fifo_throughput_limit, kms_data_key_reuse_period_seconds, kms_master_key_id, max_message_size, message_retention_seconds, name, receive_wait_time_seconds, sqs_managed_sse_enabled, tags, visibility_timeout_seconds) plus inline string fields redrive_policy and redrive_allow_policy. In the common case a single SqsQueue L1 fully replaces CfnQueue.

Optional standalone mapping for the nested CfnQueueProps.redrivePolicy JSON blob, used instead of the inline aws_sqs_queue.redrive_policy attribute specifically to break circular dependencies (e.g. two FIFO queues that redrive into each other, or a queue whose DLQ target is itself being created in the same synth) - set it out-of-band via queue_url after both queues exist. Config fields: queue_url (required), redrive_policy (required JSON string).

Optional standalone mapping for the nested CfnQueueProps.redriveAllowPolicy JSON blob, same rationale as above - lets the redrive-allow permission be attached via queue_url after the source/target queues are created, avoiding cycles. Config fields: queue_url (required), redrive_allow_policy (required JSON string).

attributeNotes:
VERIFIED against CfnQueueProps (sqs.generated.d.ts lines 145-315, all 16 props) and SqsQueueConfig (@cdktn/provider-aws sqs-queue/index.d.ts). All CfnQueueProps fields are accounted for; no gaps.

Direct 1:1 fields (name differs by case-convention only, same semantics/units):
- contentBasedDeduplication -> content_based_deduplication (bool)
- deduplicationScope -> deduplication_scope (string enum: messageGroup|queue)
- delaySeconds -> delay_seconds (int seconds, CFN range 0-900)
- fifoQueue -> fifo_queue (bool)
- fifoThroughputLimit -> fifo_throughput_limit (string enum: perQueue|perMessageGroupId)
- kmsDataKeyReusePeriodSeconds -> kms_data_key_reuse_period_seconds (int seconds, 60-86400, default 300)
- kmsMasterKeyId -> kms_master_key_id (string, alias/ARN/id)
- sqsManagedSseEnabled -> sqs_managed_sse_enabled (bool)

Fields that map 1:1 but with a renamed TF attribute (values/units identical, only the name changed):
- maximumMessageSize -> max_message_size (bytes, 1024-262144)
- messageRetentionPeriod -> message_retention_seconds (int seconds, 60-1209600, default 345600) - CFN name omits "seconds" but the value has always been seconds; TF is explicit.
- receiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds -> receive_wait_time_seconds (int seconds, 0-20)
- visibilityTimeout -> visibility_timeout_seconds (int seconds, 0-43200, default 30)
- queueName -> name (string). If queueName is omitted, CFN auto-generates a unique physical name; if name is omitted on aws_sqs_queue, AWS generates a random name, or you can use TF-only name_prefix for prefix-based generation (no CFN property equivalent). FIFO .fifo suffix requirement applies identically on both sides.

Shape/semantics differences requiring transformation:
- redrivePolicy: CfnQueueProps types this as `any | IResolvable` (a JSON object with camelCase keys deadLetterTargetArn/maxReceiveCount rendered as a JSON object in the template). TF's aws_sqs_queue.redrive_policy (and standalone aws_sqs_queue_redrive_policy.redrive_policy) is a plain JSON string (typically jsonencode({...})); key casing (deadLetterTargetArn, maxReceiveCount) is unchanged, so only the string-encoding step is new, not a key rename. Prefer the standalone resource when the DLQ target is created in the same stack with a possible reference cycle.
- redriveAllowPolicy: same treatment - CFN's `any` JSON object (redrivePermission: allowAll|denyAll|byQueue, plus sourceQueueArns) becomes a JSON string on redrive_allow_policy (inline or standalone aws_sqs_queue_redrive_allow_policy); key casing preserved.
- tags: CfnQueueProps.tags is `Array<cdk.CfnTag>` (list of {Key, Value}). aws_sqs_queue.tags is a flat `{[key: string]: string}` map - flatten Key/Value pairs into map entries. TF also exposes computed tags_all (merged with provider default_tags) with no CFN equivalent.

CFN attributes (Fn::GetAtt) -> TF computed attributes (all confirmed present on both sides):
- attrArn -> aws_sqs_queue.arn (computed)
- attrQueueUrl -> aws_sqs_queue.url (computed)
- attrQueueName -> aws_sqs_queue.name (computed if name_prefix used, otherwise echoes input name)

TF-only fields with no CfnQueueProps equivalent (leave unset / defaulted unless the source construct needs them):
- policy: full queue access-policy JSON attached directly on aws_sqs_queue. CfnQueue itself has no policy property - queue policies are a separate sibling CFN resource, AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy / AWS::SQS::QueueInlinePolicy (declared in sqs.generated.d.ts as CfnQueuePolicy/CfnQueueInlinePolicy but NOT part of CfnQueueProps). If the L2 Queue emits one alongside CfnQueue (via grant*/addToResourcePolicy), the corresponding TF resource is aws_sqs_queue_policy (dir sqs-queue-policy, fields: queue_url (required), policy (required)). Confirmed present; flagged for completeness but out of scope of the CfnQueue mapping since it isn't a CfnQueueProps property.
- region: TF provider-region override, no CFN concept.
- id / name_prefix / tags_all / timeouts (create/delete/update duration strings): TF-SDK or lifecycle conveniences with no CfnQueueProps analog.

Confidence caveat: the L1 property-surface mapping (aws_sqs_queue primary, redrive-policy/redrive-allow-policy as optional standalone) is unambiguous from the .d.ts diff; the choice between inline redrive_policy/redrive_allow_policy vs. the standalone resources is a conversion-strategy decision (cycle-avoidance), so treat that split as a recommendation, not a strict requirement.

tfResources.role: Primary (and only) mapping. Attaches a resource-based IAM policy document to a single SQS queue, identified by its queue URL. This is the direct terraform-provider-aws equivalent of CfnQueuePolicy — same conceptual resource (a standalone queue-policy attachment, not a nested/inline property of the queue itself).

attributeNotes:
Property-by-property mapping, CfnQueuePolicyProps -> SqsQueuePolicyConfig (verified against sqs.generated.d.ts lines 395-463 and sqs-queue-policy/index.d.ts SqsQueuePolicyConfig):

- `policyDocument` (any | IResolvable) -> `policy` (string, REQUIRED). SHAPE DIFFERENCE: CFN accepts a native JSON object (rendered inline in the CFN template, often built via `iam.PolicyDocument.toJSON()` in CDK) whereas the CDKTN/TF resource requires a JSON-encoded STRING. When converting, the policy document object must be serialized (e.g. with `JSON.stringify`, or better, built via a `DataAwsIamPolicyDocument` data source and referenced as `.json`, or via CDKTN's `Fn.jsonencode`) before assignment to `policy`. Preserve `Version: "2012-10-17"` in the JSON — CDK's PolicyDocument sets this by default; AWS can hang on create/update if it is missing.

- `queues` (Array<string>, list of queue URLs) -> `queue_url` (single string, REQUIRED). SHAPE/CARDINALITY DIFFERENCE — KEY MAPPING GOTCHA: CfnQueuePolicy natively supports attaching one policy document to MULTIPLE queues in a single resource (array of queue URLs). `aws_sqs_queue_policy` / CDKTN `SqsQueuePolicy` only accepts one `queueUrl` per instance. A single CfnQueuePolicy with N queues must be fanned out into N separate `SqsQueuePolicy` TF resource instances at synth time (loop over `queues`, one `SqsQueuePolicy` per URL, sharing the same rendered `policy` string), each with a distinct construct id. This is the `oneToMany` flag.

- `attrId` (CFN attribute `Id`, provider-assigned physical resource id for the queue-policy attachment; confirmed at sqs.generated.d.ts line 415) -> No semantically equivalent TF computed attribute. `aws_sqs_queue_policy` exports no additional attributes beyond config-driven ones (`id`, `policy`, `queue_url`, `region`). TF's `id` for this resource is the queue URL (used for `terraform import`), which is NOT the same as CFN's generated physical id. Any CDK code referencing `queuePolicy.attrId` (rare) has no equivalent Ref target on the TF side and should be dropped or replaced with a reference to the source `Queue.queueUrl` if that was the intent.

- `region` (TF, optional; no CFN counterpart — CFN resources are regional via the stack). Leave unset unless the CDK app explicitly targets a non-default region via cross-region provider aliasing.

- `id` (TF, optional config field, generally not set by conversion — it is the computed import id / queue URL).

- Distinguish from the sibling CFN resource `AWS::SQS::QueueInlinePolicy` (`CfnQueueInlinePolicy`, sqs.generated.d.ts lines 323-385) which takes a single `queue: string` (not an array) plus `policyDocument`; that one maps 1:1 (no fan-out) to the same `aws_sqs_queue_policy` / `SqsQueuePolicy` TF resource. Both CFN resources converge on the identical TF resource type, differentiated only by cardinality of the CFN-side queue reference.

- Not part of CfnQueuePolicy: `sqs-queue-redrive-policy` and `sqs-queue-redrive-allow-policy` map to CfnQueue's `redrivePolicy`/`redriveAllowPolicy` nested JSON properties, not to CfnQueuePolicy — do not conflate them with the queue-policy attachment resource.
